title: Bug severity runs backwards from convention, so the queue sorts backwards
body:
The bug-severity scale runs ASCENDING — S0 mildest, S4 most severe — which is the reverse
of the convention nearly every reporter arrives with, where S1 is critical and S4 is
cosmetic. Nothing at the point of entry said so: the exit-interview schema carried a bare
`z.enum(["S0","S1","S2","S3","S4"])` with no description.

Because `SEVERITY_WEIGHT` doubles at every step (S0 1, S1 2, S2 4, S3 8, S4 16), an
inverted report does not merely misrank by a little. A cosmetic nit filed as S4 outranks a
genuine defect filed as S2 by four times, so the dev loop's queue comes out close to
backwards while every individual report still reads as reasonable. Nothing anywhere
flags it.

EVIDENCE THAT IT ACTUALLY MISLEADS

I inverted it myself, in a reference-tier session, having already read this repo's audit
and its source. I filed "every option carries consequence as an empty string" — a
cosmetic data smell — as S4, and "a permanent background is committed at decision 2,
before the vocabulary its tradeoffs are written in has been taught" as S2. Triage then
sorted exactly as told: the empty-string nit came out top of the queue, ahead of the
finding about irreversible commitments.

The live two-loop run looks like it happened there too. One lead filed the MCP
empty-schema defect as S2 while calling it "the one genuinely broken tool", and filed a
silently-set flag with no narration as S4. Under the real scale the silent flag outranks
the broken tool 16 to 4, which is the opposite of that lead's own stated emphasis.

DONE ALREADY

The enum now carries a description naming the direction and warning that it reverses the
usual scale, so the next reporter reads it at the moment of filing rather than inferring
it from ranking behaviour afterwards.

STILL WORTH DECIDING

A description helps a careful reader and does nothing for a hurried one. Two options,
and this is a judgement call rather than an obvious fix:

  - Flip the scale to match convention (S1 critical … S4 cosmetic). Honest and permanent,
    but it silently reinterprets every severity already stored in the corpus, so it needs
    a migration or a schema version, not just an edit.
  - Or rename the values to something with no established opposite meaning — `trivial`,
    `minor`, `moderate`, `serious`, `severe` — which cannot be inverted because the words
    carry their own order. More churn, no ambiguity left afterwards.

The second is likelier right: the problem is that "S2" looks like it means something the
reader already knows, and no amount of documentation fully beats that.

Worth re-reading the corpus before acting either way — if most existing reports are
inverted, the stored severities are already unreliable and a migration cannot simply
trust them.

evidence.summary: S4 is most severe here but cosmetic everywhere else; a reference-tier session and at least one live-test lead both inverted it.
